shortcuts.desc: Trims elements to meet the edges of other selected elements.
steps: Type 'TR' on your keyboard and hit Enter.
Select cutting edges or press Enter to select all.
Click the parts of the lines you want to remove.
shortcuts.proTip: Hold SHIFT while using Trim to quickly extend lines instead!

shortcuts.desc: Extends lines or objects to meet the boundary edges of another object.
steps: Press 'EX' on your keyboard and press Enter.
Select boundary edges or hit Enter to pick all objects as boundaries.
Click the lines you want to extend toward the boundary.
shortcuts.proTip: Hold SHIFT while using Extend to switch into Trim mode on the fly!

shortcuts.desc: Creates a copy of a sketch line, model line, or wall at a parallel distance.
steps: Press 'OF' on your keyboard to activate the Offset tool.
Hover over the face or edges and click once.
Drag your cursor inside or outside, type the offset dimension, and hit Enter.
shortcuts.proTip: Double-click on any other face to repeat the exact same offset distance instantly!

calendar.title: F8 / ORTHO: Turn On Ortho Mode
calendar.desc: Locks your cursor to perfectly horizontal or vertical movement — the first thing every beginner should learn before drawing anything.
bullets: Press F8 to toggle Ortho mode on or off.
With Ortho on, start any draw command like LINE.
Move your mouse — notice it only snaps to 0°, 90°, 180°, or 270°.
calendar.proTip: Ortho is great for walls and straight layouts, but turn it off (F8 again) when you need angled lines.

calendar.title: F3 / OSNAP: Turn On Object Snap
calendar.desc: Makes your cursor automatically snap to precise points like endpoints, midpoints, and intersections — essential for accurate drawings.
bullets: Press F3 to toggle Object Snap on or off.
Right-click the OSNAP icon in the status bar and choose which snap points to enable (Endpoint, Midpoint, Center, Intersection are the essentials).
Start drawing — your cursor will show a colored marker when it's snapping to a precise point.
calendar.proTip: Beginners should start with just Endpoint, Midpoint, and Intersection enabled — too many snap points active at once gets confusing fast.

calendar.title: Z then Enter, or scroll wheel: Zoom In and Out
calendar.keys: Z then Enter, or scroll wheel
calendar.desc: Lets you move closer to or further from your drawing to see detail or the full layout.
bullets: Scroll the mouse wheel up to zoom in, down to zoom out.
Or type 'Z' and Enter, then type 'E' for Zoom Extents to fit your entire drawing on screen.
Type 'Z' then 'W' to zoom into a specific window you draw with two clicks.
calendar.proTip: Double-click the mouse wheel at any time to instantly zoom to fit everything in the drawing — the fastest way to get your bearings.

calendar.title: P (hold scroll wheel): Pan Around the Drawing
calendar.desc: Moves your view around the drawing without zooming, like sliding a piece of paper under your eyes.
bullets: Press and hold the mouse scroll wheel down.
Drag your mouse to slide the view in any direction.
Release the scroll wheel to stop panning.
calendar.proTip: You can also type 'P' and Enter for a dedicated Pan mode, then press Esc when done.

calendar.title: L: Draw a Line
calendar.desc: Creates a straight line segment between two or more points — the single most-used command in AutoCAD.
bullets: Type 'L' and hit Enter (or Spacebar).
Click your starting point in the drawing area.
Click your endpoint, then press Enter to finish, or keep clicking to chain multiple segments.
calendar.proTip: Hold Shift while drawing to temporarily snap to orthogonal (90°) angles, even if Ortho mode is off.

calendar.title: C: Draw a Circle
calendar.desc: Creates a circle using a center point and radius, or several other definition methods.
bullets: Type 'C' and hit Enter.
Click the center point of the circle.
Type a radius value and hit Enter, or click a point to set the radius visually.
calendar.proTip: Type '2P', '3P', or 'TTR' right after starting the command to define the circle by two points, three points, or tangent-tangent-radius instead of center+radius.

calendar.title: REC: Draw a Rectangle
calendar.desc: Creates a rectangle from two diagonal corner points in a single command.
bullets: Type 'REC' and hit Enter.
Click the first corner point.
Click the opposite corner, or type exact width/height values and hit Enter.
calendar.proTip: Type 'D' before placing the second corner to input exact dimensions instead of eyeballing it.

calendar.title: PL: Draw a Polyline
calendar.desc: Draws connected line and arc segments as a single, unified object instead of separate lines.
bullets: Type 'PL' and hit Enter.
Click your starting point, then click each subsequent point to build the shape.
Type 'C' and Enter to close the shape back to the start, or press Enter to leave it open.
calendar.proTip: Type 'W' mid-command to set a custom start/end width — great for drawing arrows or tapered walls in one go.

calendar.title: A: Draw an Arc
calendar.desc: Creates a curved segment using various combinations of start point, center, endpoint, radius, or angle.
bullets: Type 'A' and hit Enter.
Click the arc's start point.
Click a second point (or center/angle depending on method) and then the endpoint to complete the arc.
calendar.proTip: Press Enter right after drawing a line to auto-continue into an arc tangent to that line — no need to restart the command.

calendar.title: E: Erase an Object
calendar.desc: Deletes selected objects from your drawing — the most basic cleanup command there is.
bullets: Click the object(s) you want to remove (or type 'E' first, then select).
Type 'E' and hit Enter if you selected first.
Press Enter to confirm the selection and delete it.
calendar.proTip: Just pressing the Delete key on your keyboard after selecting objects works exactly the same — no need to type E at all.

calendar.title: U: Undo Your Last Action
calendar.desc: Reverses your most recent command — the most important safety net when you're learning.
bullets: Type 'U' and hit Enter, or press Ctrl+Z.
Repeat to undo multiple steps back through your history.
Use 'REDO' (or Ctrl+Y) if you undid one step too many.
calendar.proTip: Don't be afraid to experiment — U/Ctrl+Z can always bring you back, so there's no real way to permanently break a drawing while learning.

calendar.title: M: Move an Object
calendar.desc: Relocates selected objects from one point to another without changing their size or rotation.
bullets: Select the object(s) you want to move.
Type 'M' and hit Enter.
Click a base point, then click the destination point (or type a distance and direction).
calendar.proTip: Use a precise Object Snap point (like a corner) as your base point so the move lines up exactly where you intend.

calendar.title: CO / CP: Copy an Object
calendar.desc: Duplicates selected objects to a new location, leaving the original in place.
bullets: Select the object(s) you want to copy.
Type 'CO' and hit Enter.
Click a base point, then click each destination point — keep clicking to place multiple copies, press Enter to finish.
calendar.proTip: Since Copy repeats automatically for multiple placements, you don't need to restart the command for each duplicate.

calendar.title: RO: Rotate an Object
calendar.desc: Turns selected objects around a chosen base point by a specific angle.
bullets: Select the object(s) you want to rotate.
Type 'RO' and hit Enter.
Click the base point to rotate around, then type an angle (or click to rotate visually) and hit Enter.
calendar.proTip: Type 'C' before confirming the angle to create a rotated copy instead of rotating the original in place.

calendar.title: MI: Mirror an Object
calendar.desc: Creates a flipped duplicate of selected objects across a line you define.
bullets: Select the object(s) you want to mirror.
Type 'MI' and hit Enter.
Click two points to define the mirror line, then choose whether to keep or delete the original.
calendar.proTip: Use Ortho mode (F8) while picking the mirror line to guarantee a perfectly horizontal or vertical flip.

calendar.title: O: Offset an Object
calendar.desc: Creates a parallel copy of a line, polyline, or curve at a specified distance.
bullets: Type 'O' and hit Enter.
Type the offset distance and hit Enter.
Click the object to offset, then click the side you want the copy to appear on.
calendar.proTip: Use the 'Multiple' option to place several offset copies at the same distance without restarting the command each time.

calendar.title: TR: Trim Objects
calendar.desc: Trims elements to meet the edges of other selected elements — one of the most-used editing commands.
bullets: Type 'TR' and hit Enter.
Select cutting edges (optional), or press Enter to use all visible objects as boundaries.
Click the parts of the lines you want to remove.
calendar.proTip: Hold Shift while using Trim to instantly extend lines instead — no need to switch commands.

calendar.title: EX: Extend Objects
calendar.desc: Stretches a line, arc, or polyline until it meets another selected boundary object.
bullets: Type 'EX' and hit Enter.
Select the boundary edge(s), or press Enter to use all visible objects.
Click the object you want to extend, near the end that should stretch.
calendar.proTip: Just like Trim, hold Shift while in Extend to instantly switch to trimming instead.

calendar.title: F: Fillet Two Lines
calendar.desc: Rounds (or squares off) the corner where two lines meet, using a specified radius.
bullets: Type 'F' and hit Enter.
Type 'R' to set a radius value (use 0 for a sharp clean corner).
Click the first line, then click the second line to complete the corner.
calendar.proTip: Set the radius to 0 for an instant clean square corner — much faster than manually trimming and extending two lines.

calendar.title: CHA: Chamfer Two Lines
calendar.desc: Creates a beveled (angled) corner between two lines instead of a sharp or rounded one.
bullets: Type 'CHA' and hit Enter.
Type 'D' to set two distance values for the bevel.
Click the first line, then click the second line to complete the chamfer.
calendar.proTip: Use Chamfer for structural steel connection details — it's the standard way to represent a beveled edge in fabrication drawings.

calendar.title: SC: Scale an Object
calendar.desc: Resizes selected objects uniformly larger or smaller from a chosen base point.
bullets: Select the object(s) you want to resize.
Type 'SC' and hit Enter.
Click the base point, then type a scale factor (e.g. 2 for double size, 0.5 for half) and hit Enter.
calendar.proTip: Type 'R' (Reference) instead of a raw number to scale an object to match an existing reference length — AutoCAD calculates the ratio for you.

calendar.title: S: Stretch an Object
calendar.desc: Moves part of an object while keeping the rest connected — used to resize shapes without redrawing them.
bullets: Type 'S' and hit Enter.
Draw a crossing selection window that only captures the part you want to move (not the whole object).
Click a base point, then click the destination point.
calendar.proTip: Stretch only moves what's fully or partially inside your crossing window — objects fully outside it won't move at all, which is what makes it useful.

calendar.title: AR: Array an Object (Rectangular/Polar/Path)
calendar.desc: Creates multiple evenly-spaced copies of an object in a grid, circular pattern, or along a path.
bullets: Select the object(s) you want to array.
Type 'AR' and hit Enter, then choose Rectangular, Polar, or Path.
Set the number of copies and spacing/angle, then press Enter to confirm.
calendar.proTip: Arrays stay associative by default — editing one item or the spacing later updates the entire array automatically.

calendar.title: LA: Open Layer Manager
calendar.desc: Controls the organization of your drawing into named layers with their own color, linetype, and visibility.
bullets: Type 'LA' and hit Enter to open the Layer Properties Manager.
Click 'New Layer' to create one, then rename it and assign a color.
Use the layer dropdown in the ribbon to set which layer is 'current' before drawing new objects.
calendar.proTip: Always draw on a specifically-named layer (never Layer 0) — it keeps your drawing organized and makes printing/plotting far easier to control.

calendar.title: MT: Add Multiline Text
calendar.desc: Inserts a paragraph-style text box that wraps automatically, used for notes and longer annotations.
bullets: Type 'MT' and hit Enter.
Click and drag to define the width of the text box.
Type your text, then click outside the box (or press the Close button) to finish.
calendar.proTip: Use the in-place Text Editor ribbon that appears to change font, size, or add bullet points without leaving the command.

calendar.title: DLI: Add a Linear Dimension
calendar.desc: Places a horizontal or vertical dimension line showing the exact distance between two points.
bullets: Type 'DLI' and hit Enter.
Click the first extension line origin point.
Click the second point, then click to place the dimension line at your desired offset distance.
calendar.proTip: Use Object Snap (F3) to click exact endpoints — dimensions snapped to precise points stay accurate if the geometry later changes.

calendar.title: H: Add a Hatch Pattern
calendar.desc: Fills an enclosed area with a repeating pattern — commonly used to represent materials like concrete, insulation, or earth.
bullets: Type 'H' and hit Enter.
Choose a hatch pattern from the ribbon that appears (e.g. ANSI31 for concrete/steel sections).
Click inside the enclosed area you want to fill, then press Enter to confirm.
calendar.proTip: Make sure the boundary is a fully closed shape first — Hatch will fail or leak into unintended areas if there's even a tiny gap.

calendar.title: B: Create a Block
calendar.desc: Bundles multiple objects into a single reusable component, like a door symbol or furniture icon.
bullets: Draw the geometry you want to turn into a block.
Type 'B' and hit Enter, then name your block.
Click 'Select Objects', select your geometry, pick a base/insertion point, and click OK.
calendar.proTip: Always pick a logical, snappable base point (like a corner) — it makes inserting the block later far more precise.

calendar.title: I: Insert a Block
calendar.desc: Places a previously created block (or another drawing file) into your current drawing.
bullets: Type 'I' and hit Enter to open the Insert dialog.
Select the block you want to place from the list.
Click in the drawing to place it, adjusting scale/rotation if needed before confirming.
calendar.proTip: Type the block name directly at the command line after 'I' if you already know it — faster than browsing the dialog every time.

calendar.title: MO / PR: Open the Properties Palette
calendar.desc: Shows and lets you edit every property (layer, color, linetype, dimensions) of a selected object in one panel.
bullets: Select an object in your drawing.
Type 'MO' or 'PR' and hit Enter (or press Ctrl+1).
Edit any value directly in the palette — changes apply instantly to the selected object.
calendar.proTip: Keep this palette pinned open while learning — it's the fastest way to understand exactly what properties any object actually has.

calendar.title: MA: Match Properties
calendar.desc: Copies all formatting (layer, color, linetype) from one object onto others in a single click — like a paintbrush tool.
bullets: Type 'MA' and hit Enter.
Click the source object whose properties you want to copy.
Click each target object you want to match — press Enter when finished.
calendar.proTip: Right-click before finishing to open Settings and choose exactly which properties get copied (e.g. only layer, not linetype).

calendar.title: Ctrl+P: Plot / Print Your Drawing
calendar.desc: Sends your drawing to a printer or exports it as a PDF, the final step of finishing any drawing.
bullets: Press Ctrl+P (or type 'PLOT' and hit Enter).
Choose your printer or 'DWG to PDF.pc3' to export as a PDF.
Set the paper size and scale, preview the result, then click OK to plot.
calendar.proTip: Always click 'Preview' before the final plot — it catches missing lines, wrong scale, or cut-off content before you waste paper or send a bad PDF.
